The image shows a corn seedling/young plant being held, with the stalk split open showing internal tissue. I can see:
- Dark brown/black discoloration at the crown/node area
- Some grayish-white material around the crown/roots
- Fibrous roots extending from the crown
- The stem appears to have been split longitudinally revealing internal discoloration

This looks like a stalk/crown rot disease. Let me examine reference images for top candidates.

None of those match the test image. The test image shows a young corn seedling with:
- Stalk split open at crown level
- Dark brownish-black node discoloration at crown
- Grayish/white fuzzy material around the crown/nodes (possible fungal sporulation)
- Small fibrous roots

This looks like early crown infection — the gray fuzzy material could be downy mildew-like sporangiophores. Let me check one more reference image to confirm.

The Anthracnose_stalk_rot top-right panel actually shows some similarity (split stalk with dark node discoloration), but the test image shows a much younger seedling at the crown/root level with gray fuzzy material that looks more like fungal sporulation.

**Key visual analysis:**
- Very young corn seedling (V1-V2 stage) held between fingers
- Stalk split at crown, showing internal tissue
- **Dark brown-black discoloration at crown nodes** — consistent with node infection
- **Gray/white fuzzy material at crown level** — could be downy mildew-like sporangiophores
- Fibrous roots extending from crown

The gray fluffy material at the crown nodes of a young seedling, combined with early node discoloration, is characteristic of **Crazy_top** (*Sclerophthora macrospora*) — which infects through roots in waterlogged conditions at the seedling stage and produces downy white-gray sporulation at the crown before later developing into the characteristic tassel proliferations. This is a diagnostic image taken before the canopy-level symptoms appear.
